answer: Each identity must bind itself to one physical chip through a quartz-oscillator PUF fingerprint: at dawn the network beacon issues a fresh challenge, and the chip answers with its unique timing signature, verified against its registered fingerprint. One chip yields one identity, so a sybil farmer must buy a separate chip per fake identity at $12 each plus a $3 beacon registration fee, making the cost grow linearly — ten fakes cost $150, a hundred cost $1,500.
